dressing.name: The Ashen Crypt
dressing.overview: A single burial chamber beneath a ruined chapel. Cold, close. The stair they came down is south; an open door leads north.
dressing.sensory: Air like a held breath. The braziers hiss. Every sound arrives a half-second late, as if the room is deciding whether to allow it.

propDescriptions.stair-south: The stair the party came down, open to the grey light of the ruin above.
propDescriptions.brazier-east: A second brazier, matching the first, its flame guttering as if in a draught you cannot feel.
propDescriptions.candles-north: A huddle of candles on the north wall, burned down to nubs.
propDescriptions.banner-east: A faded banner on the east wall, the device worn to a stain.
propDescriptions.fox: A stone fox, sitting, watching the north door. One ear is broken off.
propDescriptions.barrel-west: A warped barrel shoved against the west wall, its hoops rusted shut.
propDescriptions.crate-east: A splintered crate, empty except for straw gone to dust.
propDescriptions.lantern-north: A standing lantern, unlit, between the east brazier and the north wall.
propDescriptions.pillar-west: A squat pillar, its base ringed with old wax.
propDescriptions.skull-north: A yellowed skull on the flagstones, missing the jaw.
propDescriptions.sarcophagus: A stone sarcophagus on a low dais. The lid is carved with a robed figure whose face has been deliberately chiselled away. The seam is scored with fresh scratches, as though something has worked at it from beneath.
propDescriptions.horse: A horse statue, smaller than life, its rider long since knocked away.
propDescriptions.brazier-west: An iron brazier burning low and green. It gives heat but no smoke.
propDescriptions.door-north: A slab door on the north wall, banded in tarnished iron. It stands open.
propDescriptions.alcove: A shallow alcove behind a displaced stone, holding a clay votive lamp and a bundle of grave-cloth gone black with age.
propDescriptions.shrine-north: A small shrine jammed into the north-east corner, its niche empty.
propDescriptions.bucket-west: An iron bucket beside the west brazier, dry.
propDescriptions.chair-north: A wooden chair facing the north door, as if someone had been waiting.
propDescriptions.coffin-corner: A plain coffin stood on end in the corner, the lid still nailed.
propDescriptions.vase-east: A tall vase, chipped at the lip, holding nothing but grit.
propDescriptions.pot-west: A clay pot, the kind grave-goods come in, its mouth sealed with wax.
propDescriptions.pillar-east: A squat pillar. Something has scratched a tally into it — eleven marks, the last one incomplete.
propDescriptions.rubble: A spill of fallen masonry where the ceiling has given way.
propDescriptions.ribcage-east: A ribcage, animal or child, it is hard to say, slumped against the east wall.
propDescriptions.cobweb-west: A thick cobweb spanning the west wall, grey with dust.

text: The cold hits first, thick with the smell of turned earth and old tallow.
Twin braziers hiss low on either side of the chamber, casting a greasy green light over the defaced sarcophagus at the center. Ahead, an iron-banded door stands already open to the dark.
I inspect the sarcophagus

name: roll_check
message: investigation check, DC 15. Rolled 10 +0 = 10 — FAILURE. Narrate this outcome and commit to it.

text: You run your fingers along the pitted rim of the heavy lid, finding only gritty lime and old chisel-bites.
The pale gouges along the seam show something clawed at the stone from within, but the heavy slab remains entirely unyielding under your hands.
Whatever else might be hidden among the carvings stays lost in the green-lit gloom.
Fingers found only gritty lime and old chisel-bites along the sarcophagus rim.

message: Recorded: The seam shows clawed scratches from something trapped beneath.

text: I try to shove the lid open

name: roll_check
message: athletics check, DC 20. Rolled 16 +5 = 21 — SUCCESS. Narrate this outcome and commit to it.

text: You brace your boots against the dais and put your whole weight into the cold stone.

With a sharp, grinding screech that echoes off the vaulting, the slab shifts aside, releasing a waft of stale air from the dark interior. The heavy lid hangs half-cocked over the rim, its ancient seal broken.
The sarcophagus lid is half-cocked open, its ancient seal broken.

name: assert_fact
argumentsJson: {"text": "The sarcophagus lid is half-cocked open, its ancient seal broken.", "anchor": "on", "x": null, "y": null, "target_id": "sarcophagus"}
message: Recorded: The sarcophagus lid is half-cocked open, its ancient seal broken.

text: i look inside

name: roll_check
message: investigation check, DC 15. Rolled 19 +0 = 19 — SUCCESS. Narrate this outcome and commit to it.

name: spawn_entity
message: A goblin is now on the grid at (6,7). Describe its arrival.

name: move_entity
message: Moved 'fighter' to (6,6).

text: You peer past the shifted lid to find only grey bone-meal, but something suddenly explodes outward in a flurry of chalky dust.
A wiry goblin scrabbles out of the stone trough, spitting grit and baring a notched blade in the green glare. The sudden lunge forces you back a step as the creature finds its footing atop the tomb.

name: spawn_entity
message: REJECTED: (6,7) is already occupied — pick another square

text: I ask "what filth lay here?" in disgust

name: roll_check
message: persuasion check, DC 15. Rolled 19 +2 = 21 — SUCCESS. Narrate this outcome and commit to it.

text: "What filth lay here?"
The creature cowers atop the slab, lowering the notched sword as it wipes a smear of grey dust from its snout.
"Not filth, just Vessk—was only hiding from the noises up above!"

name: move_entity
message: REJECTED: Something solid is already at 6,7

text: I ask "what noises? what did you hear?"

name: roll_check
message: persuasion check, DC 10. Rolled 1 +2 = 3 — FAILURE. Narrate this outcome and commit to it.

text: "What noises? What did you hear?"
Vessk's yellow eyes dart to your drawn steel, his jaw snapping shut as he presses his back hard against the tomb's stone lip.
"Tricks! You want Vessk to look away so you poke him!"
"I'll poke you if you don't tell me what you know!"

name: roll_check
message: persuasion check, DC 15. Rolled 1 +2 = 3 — FAILURE. Narrate this outcome and commit to it.

text: "I'll poke you if you don't tell me what you know!"
Vessk bares his needle teeth, spitting in the dust and tightening his white-knuckled grip on the notched blade.
Your torch gutters with a sickly hiss, pulling the shadows tight around your boots as the green brazier-light swallows the edges of the room.
"fine so be it", I now attack the goblin with my sword

name: start_combat
message: Combat has begun. Initiative order: Roderick (18), Vessk (8). Describe only the instant the fight breaks out — one or two sentences. Do not list the order. Do not narrate anyone's turn, attack, movement or wound: none of that has happened yet.

text: "Fine, so be it."
Your blade clears its scabbard with a cold scrape of iron, catching the pale green glare of the braziers.
Vessk drops low on the stone slab, baring his yellow teeth as his notched sword comes up to meet you.
Vessk scrambles off the stone dais, closing the gap with a skittering rush across the flags.
He hacks wildly at your midsection, but the notched blade whistles harmlessly through empty air as you lean clear.
Your blade bites deep through boiled leather and bone, the violent impact lifting the goblin off his heels.
Vessk crashes dead against the flags in a cloud of chalky grave-dust, his notched sword clattering across the stones.
I check his body for anything useful

name: roll_check
message: investigation check, DC 5. Rolled 17 +0 = 17 — SUCCESS. Narrate this outcome and commit to it.

text: You turn Vessk's limp body over with your boot, the smell of copper and grave-mold thick in the cold air.
His filthy pockets yield only dry moss, a few cracked chicken bones, and the notched shortsword that lies beside his curled fingers. There is nothing else of value on him.

name: move_entity
message: Moved 'fighter' to (4,5).

text: I look inside the sarcophagus now that vessk is gone
You lean over the displaced stone lid and peer into the deep trough.
A bed of stale bone-meal and a few scuffed goblin bootprints are all that settle in the bottom of the empty box.
The scratching has ended, leaving only the quiet hiss of the green braziers.
The sarcophagus contains a bed of stale bone-meal and a few scuffed goblin bootprints.

dressing.name: The Long Gallery
dressing.overview: A processional gallery, long and narrow, running north from the crypt stair. Four pillars line the aisle. An open doorway at the far end continues north.
dressing.sensory: Dry where the crypt was damp, and much colder. Dust hangs in the air where the ceiling has come down. Footsteps carry the whole length and come back.

propDescriptions.niche: A niche behind a facing stone, at knee height. It holds a stack of six clay tokens, each stamped with the same procession as the far pillars.
propDescriptions.door-north: An open doorway at the head of the gallery. Nothing bars it.
propDescriptions.pillar-near-west: A fluted pillar, first of a line of four. Something has been chiselled off it at shoulder height, thoroughly, leaving a pale scar.
propDescriptions.pillar-far-east: The fourth. Its figures walk south too, and the last of them has no head.
propDescriptions.brazier-head: A cold brazier at the head of the gallery, choked with grey ash. Whatever burned here burned out a long time before the green fires downstairs were lit.
propDescriptions.ceiling-fall: A cone of fallen ceiling, tiles and mortar, with the dust long settled into it.
propDescriptions.pillar-near-east: Its partner across the aisle, scarred in the same place and the same way.
propDescriptions.pillar-far-west: The third pillar. This one still carries its carving: a procession of small robed figures, all walking south.
propDescriptions.door-south: The slab door back to the crypt, standing open.

text: The air in the gallery is bone-dry and bite-cold, smelling of old lime and pulverized slate.

Your bootheels strike the stones and the sound clatters the full length of the aisle, past four scarred pillars toward the dark doorway at the northern end. Somewhere in the deep gloom beyond, something shifts with a dry scrape and falls instantly still.
I stay still and try to listen intently for a potential stalker

name: roll_check
message: perception check, DC 15. Rolled 5 +3 = 8 — FAILURE. Narrate this outcome and commit to it.

text: You hold your breath and strain into the cold dark, but the high vaulted ceiling turns your own pulse into a dull, thudding echo.
The draft whistles faintly through the northern doorway, masking any scrape of claw or boot against the stone. If something is moving out there, the vast silence of the gallery swallows it whole.

dressing.name: The Chapel
dressing.overview: A chapel cut into the stone, narrower than the gallery. A shrine stands in the west aisle with a small reliquary before it. Sconces line the walls, cold. An open door north, an open door south.
dressing.sensory: Wax and old incense. The air is still. When someone moves, the cold sconces seem to listen.

propDescriptions.pillar-south-east: A chapel pillar, its capital chewed by damp.
propDescriptions.reliquary: A small iron-bound reliquary, set before the shrine. The latch yields to a touch.
propDescriptions.niche: A shallow niche behind the shrine, holding a folded strip of cloth and a cracked votive.
propDescriptions.door-north: An open doorway north. Nothing bars it.
propDescriptions.banner-east: A faded chapel banner, the saint's face washed out.
propDescriptions.pillar-north-east: Its partner toward the north door, the carving worn to a suggestion of wings.
propDescriptions.chair: A wooden chair facing the shrine, as if someone had been at prayer.
propDescriptions.lantern: A standing lantern, unlit, by the north-east corner.
propDescriptions.shrine: A shrine in the west aisle, its niche empty except for a smear of old wax.
propDescriptions.cobweb: A cobweb spanning the west wall, grey with chapel dust.
propDescriptions.door-south: The doorway back to the gallery, standing open.
propDescriptions.candles-west: A huddle of unlit candles on the north-west wall.

text: The air here is close, thick with the dead grease of cold wax and ancient, stale incense.
Across the stone floor, an empty shrine stands in the west aisle with a small iron-bound reliquary resting before its niche.
To the north, another open doorway gapes black in the stillness, while unlit sconces along the walls seem to watch your guttering torchlight pass.
"ah this is the reliquary I was sent to retrieve!" I carefully inspect for traps and see if I can safely take the reliquary

name: roll_check
message: investigation check, DC 10. Rolled 13 +0 = 13 — SUCCESS. Narrate this outcome and commit to it.

text: "Ah, this is the reliquary I was sent to retrieve!"
You run your fingertips over the cold iron banding, checking the seams and the flagstones beneath for pressure plates, tension wires, or hidden needles.
The simple iron latch lifts cleanly without a hitch or a click, leaving the reliquary resting entirely untrapped and ready for the taking.
I pick it up and put it in my bag

name: take_prop
message: Took 'reliquary'. The party is carrying it.

text: The small iron-bound box is heavy with lead and cold to the touch as you lift it from the stone.
It settles into your pack with a dull clink of buckles, shifting the balance of your kit against your shoulders.
The empty space before the shrine leaves only a circle of pale dust where the box had sat for years.
The reliquary has been removed from the shrine.

name: assert_fact
argumentsJson: {"text": "The reliquary has been removed from the shrine.", "anchor": "on", "x": null, "y": null, "target_id": "shrine"}
message: Recorded: The reliquary has been removed from the shrine.

text: The gallery stretches back out before you, colder now and smelling of freshly disturbed lime.

Your failing torch flickers low against the aisle, shrinking your circle of light to the reach of your sword arm as a thin draught curls from somewhere that was shut. To the south, the open doorway to the crypt waits through the gloom.
Your torch dies to a black wick just as your boots find the crypt floor, plunging the chamber into dead, sunless dark.
The hiss of the braziers is gone, their green fires snuffed out, leaving only the sharp bite of freezing stone.
From the shadow near the sarcophagus comes the rasp of an iron blade sliding across grit, and the wet, hurried breath of something small.
I shout "who's there?"

name: roll_check
message: persuasion check, DC 15. Rolled 6 +2 = 8 — FAILURE. Narrate this outcome and commit to it.

text: "Who's there?"
Your shout crashes flat against the vaulting and dies on the cold stone.
From the gloom by the sarcophagus, a frantic rustle of cloth and the scrape of a notched blade answer instead, shifting forward into the dark.
"I thought I killed you Vessk!"
"I thought I killed you, Vessk!"
"Not dead, not dead!"
the goblin spits, baring needle teeth from the shadows beside the stone box.
He shifts his grip on the notched shortsword, dirt showering from his greasy rags as his yellow eyes fix on your chest.
Vessk lunges out of the gloom, boots slapping hard against the flagstones as he closes the gap. His notched shortsword whistles harmlessly through the empty air, carving wide of your shoulder.
Your blade drives hard through leather and bone, taking him in the chest with the blunt crack of a splitting plank.
Vessk drops his notched sword and collapses forward onto the freezing flagstones, dead before his knees hit the grit.
I frantically pull out another torch from my pack
Your flint strikes twice in the dark, sending orange sparks raining down into the pitch before the torch head catches with a sudden *whoosh*.
The blooming amber flame pushes back the gloom, casting long, sharp shadows across the floor and revealing two dead goblins sprawled motionless in the dust.
The chamber settles into heavy silence, the only sound the crackle of burning pine pitch.
Flint sparks struck here, igniting the torch

text: You step over to the spot by the sarcophagus, the torch held low so its yellow light washes across the stone.
Black soot stains the flagstones where the flint bit hard into the floor, faint wisps of acrid smoke still rising from the cold rock.
All around the mark lies the stillness of the crypt, thick with ash and the stink of spent pitch.
Black soot stains the flagstones where the flint struck.

text: You turn your back on the cold dark of the crypt and climb the south stair, the weight of the reliquary heavy in your hands.
The grey daylight of the ruined chapel breaks over you, carrying the clean smell of wind and wet pine. Behind you, the crypt holds only shadows and the quiet dust.
